title: Autotask PSA playbook failure tickets
use_case: Open a Autotask PSA ticket when a playbook run fails or finishes with the outcome FAIL, or when Sophos Fusion raises a health event such as Collector Down, naming the playbook, the error and the tenant.
trigger: Platform Events, source Playbook Execution, events failed and completed, with the Only When filter in SETUP.md, which skips runs a Playbook Execution event started. For health events, configure it again on Platform Events, source Health, event create. SETUP.md has both filters.
connections: Unofficial_AutotaskPSA 1.0.0, the Autotask PSA connector from this library: an API user's secret, user name and integration code
requires: Autotask PSA with an API user that can create tickets, and Sophos Fusion playbooks under Security Operations > Automations
mdr_note: Sophos MDR doesn't run or watch this playbook, and it doesn't change what Sophos MDR does. It opens tickets about every playbook run in the tenant, so check who sees the ticket's company.
rollback: Close or delete the tickets in Autotask PSA. Turn the playbook off to stop new ones.
author: Aaronjacobs000
summary: This playbook opens a Autotask PSA ticket when a playbook run fails or finishes with the outcome FAIL, and when Sophos Fusion raises a health event such as Collector Down. The ticket names the playbook, its template, the error and the tenant. It runs on Playbook Execution and Health events and calls the library's Autotask PSA connector, so it needs that connector and an API user that can create tickets.
notes:
Setup:
- One configured playbook takes one trigger, so set it up once for Playbook Execution and again for Health if you want both.
- Company ID, Queue ID, Priority and New ticket status are picklist numbers that vary by Autotask account. For a partner-level playbook, Company by tenant maps each Sophos Fusion tenant ID to its company.
- Pair it with Playbook failure alerts to post to chat as well. It opens tickets only, so it has no dry run.

How it works:
- The ticket carries the same text as Playbook failure alerts, plus the tenant's name and ID.
- It never acts on a run that a Playbook Execution event started, on the library's playbook failure playbooks or on Sophos's Send Notification Message templates, so a failed ticket can't start another.

Testing:
- On 2026-11-15 a renamed copy, with a renamed copy of its connector imported for the check, passed playbookValidateDSLV2 with no errors or warnings in a Sophos Fusion test tenant.
- In that tenant the copy ran on real Playbook Execution events for a failed run and a run that finished with the outcome FAIL. It built the ticket with the company mapped by tenant, the queue, priority, status and a due date 24 hours on, and called Autotask PSA, which refused the made-up connection's credential (401). The run finished FAIL with that error, and the loop guard held.

Known gaps:
- Not run against a real Autotask PSA account: no ticket was created.
- No real health event happened in the test tenants during testing, so the health path ran by hand on a made-up Collector Down event in the documented shape.
- A playbook that catches an error and sets no outcome finishes Completed with the outcome UNKNOWN, and isn't caught.
- It opens or posts once per failed run. A playbook that fails on every event posts every time until you turn it off or add it to Playbooks to ignore.
